question: What is the primary purpose of diet therapy in clinical nursing care?

options.A: Accelerating the discharge rate of surgical patients
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital food services
options.C: Eliminating the need for pharmaceutical interventions
options.D: Modifying nutritional intake to manage health conditions

explanation: Diet therapy alters a patient's normal diet to support healing and disease management. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h1)

question: Why must cultural food preferences be considered when planning diet therapy?

options.A: To ensure the patient actually eats the prescribed food
options.B: To simplify the work of the attending dietitian
options.C: To comply with international hospital accreditation standards
options.D: To reduce the financial burden on the hospital kitchen

explanation: Patients are more likely to adhere to therapeutic diets that incorporate familiar and culturally accepted foods. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h1)

question: Mid-upper arm circumference is an example of which nutritional assessment category?
explanation: Anthropometric measurements involve physical body dimensions such as weight, height, and arm circumference. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h2)

question: What does a low serum albumin level primarily indicate during a nutritional assessment?

options.A: Excessive carbohydrate intake over a long period
options.C: Normal physiological adaptation to hospital rest

explanation: Serum albumin is a key biochemical marker that drops during protein depletion or severe inflammatory states. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h2)

question: A patient with severe heart failure is most likely to receive which type of therapeutic diet?
explanation: Restricting sodium intake helps prevent fluid retention and reduces the workload on a failing heart. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h3)

question: When is a mechanical soft diet typically prescribed for a hospitalized patient?

options.A: When the patient requires rapid weight loss before surgery
options.B: When the patient has difficulty chewing or swallowing
options.C: When the patient recovers from uncomplicated malaria
options.D: When the patient has acute kidney injury requiring dialysis

explanation: Mechanical soft diets feature foods altered in texture to ease chewing and swallowing for vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of diet therapy for a patient with type 2 diabetes?

options.B: Eliminating all forms of dietary fat

explanation: Diabetic meal planning focuses on consistent carbohydrate intake to prevent dangerous spikes or drops in blood sugar. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h4)

question: Why is dietary protein restricted in advanced chronic kidney disease?

options.A: To encourage rapid weight loss in obese patients
options.B: To lower elevated systemic blood pressure
options.C: To minimize the buildup of toxic waste products in the blood
options.D: To prevent the sudden onset of peripheral edema

explanation: Failing kidneys cannot clear protein breakdown byproducts efficiently, leading to toxic accumulation if intake is high. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h4)

question: What is Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food primarily used for in primary health care?

options.A: Treating acute dehydration from watery diarrhea
options.B: Supplementing iron levels in pregnant women
options.C: Preventing seasonal malaria in infants and toddlers
options.D: Treating severe acute malnutrition in community settings

explanation: RUTF is a specialized, calorie-dense paste designed for outpatient rehabilitation of severely malnourished children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h5)

question: A community health nurse uses which tool for rapid malnutrition screening during outreach?
explanation: MUAC tapes provide a fast, reliable, and portable way to screen for acute malnutrition in field environments. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h5)

question: Why should family members be included during nutritional counseling sessions?

options.A: Hospital policy mandates family participation in all treatment plans
options.B: They are usually responsible for buying and preparing the household meals
options.C: Doctors require family consent for dietary modifications
options.D: Patients have poor memory retention during illness

explanation: Involving the person who cooks ensures the prescribed diet is realistically implemented at home. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h6)

question: A patient cannot afford the foreign food items on their meal plan. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Insist that the patient find extra money to buy the prescribed items
options.B: Report the patient to the hospital social welfare unit immediately
options.C: Discontinue all diet counseling since compliance is unlikely
options.D: Help the patient identify affordable, locally available food substitutes

explanation: Adapting the meal plan to local socioeconomic realities improves adherence and nutritional outcomes. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h6)

question: What is the best way to evaluate the effectiveness of a dietary intervention over time?

options.A: Monitoring clinical, anthropometric, and biochemical indicators
options.B: Checking the frequency of nursing shift handovers
options.C: Reviewing the total cost of food purchased by the ward
options.D: Asking the patient if they enjoyed the hospital meals

explanation: Objective evaluation requires tracking physical measurements, lab values, and clinical signs of recovery. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h7)

question: What should the nurse do if a patient's nutritional goals are not being met during diet therapy?

options.A: Assume the underlying disease is completely incurable
options.B: Double the prescribed nutrient restrictions without consulting the doctor
options.C: Reassess compliance and investigate hidden barriers to adherence
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately to free up ward space

explanation: Failing to meet goals prompts a review of whether the patient understands, accepts, or can afford the diet. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h7)
